fact: The document states that POPIA prohibits transfers of personal information outside South Africa unless the recipient is under adequate legal protection, or the data subject consents, or a contract or the data subject's interest requires it; POPIA took effect in July 2020 with a grace period to 30 June 2021 (event date taken from the commencement it states).

The document, published 2024-01-17 (no other date given), states that POPIA does not specify the countries with adequate protection or create a mechanism for regulatory recognition of such countries, so the transferring party must judge adequacy itself.

A DCDT presentation to Parliament's communications committee, dated 24 February 2026, states that the National Data and Cloud Policy provides that government data carrying content on national security and the sovereignty of the Republic shall be stored only in digital infrastructure located within South Africa's borders.
